subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
passage: Uday, since you asked about my blushing: it's the worst in assembly. Last term, the teacher asked me to read the morning thought. As soon as I walked to the microphone my face went hot, and I was sure that the whole hall was staring at my red cheeks. My heart was banging. What helped was small things. I breathed out slowly, longer than I breathed in. I looked at the page and at the back wall instead of watching myself in my head. And I reminded myself that most people are thinking about their own morning, not my face. I still turned red, and I read all the same. I'm Pallavi, by the way. Afterwards nobody said a word about it.

qa.q: Where is the blushing the worst for Pallavi?
qa.a: It is the worst in assembly.

qa.q: What was Pallavi afraid of at the microphone?
qa.a: Pallavi was afraid the whole hall was staring at those red cheeks, which fed the anxiety and the banging heart.

qa.q: What steps helped Pallavi while blushing?
qa.a: Pallavi breathed out slowly, looked at the page and the back wall, and remembered that most people were thinking about their own morning.

qa.q: How might the students in the hall have seen Pallavi?
qa.a: Most were probably busy with their own thoughts, so they likely didn't notice the blush as much as Pallavi feared.

grounding: A teen who blushes easily fears being noticed, and slow breathing, focusing outward and remembering most people don't notice help.

subtopic: Visible reactions with multiple possible causes
passage: Payal got asked a question in biology, and I was sitting right behind her. She went red from her collar up to her ears. I saw her put down her pen and take one long breath out, then another. She looked at the diagram on the board rather than at anyone, and I heard her say, "Could you repeat the question, Miss?" Her voice was small but steady. She answered correctly. Afterwards she pressed the back of her hand to her cheek and gave a short laugh. I can't tell if she was frightened, or just hot, or embarrassed. She seemed to calm down after a bit. Nobody around us even glanced at her. - Indu

qa.q: What did Payal ask the teacher after she was called on?
qa.a: She asked the teacher to repeat the question.

qa.q: What might Payal have been feeling when she blushed?
qa.a: She was probably anxious about being looked at, shown by the long breaths and looking at the board, though Indu admits it could also have been heat or embarrassment.
Slow breaths and focusing on the diagram instead of the faces around her.

qa.q: How did the other students seem to see Payal's blush?
qa.a: Indu notes that nobody around them even glanced at her, which fits the idea that most people don't notice as much as the blusher fears.

grounding: A teen who blushes easily fears being noticed, and slow breathing and focusing outward help.
